issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a method named printFarmSong(), but the provided template and the reference solution use a method named singFarmSong(). This name mismatch between the specification and the codebase can confuse students about which method to implement and which name tests or Main expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either update the problem statement to instruct implementation of singFarmSong(), or rename the template and solution methods to printFarmSong() (and keep singFarmSong() as a deprecated alias if backward compatibility is desired). Ensure Main and any tests reference the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a Farm method named printFarmSong(), but both the template and the solution implement and reference a method named singFarmSong(). This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual operation (playing/printing the farm song) can confuse students about which method to implement or call and may lead to mismatches with test expectations.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across artifacts. Either (A) change the problem statement and UML to refer to singFarmSong(), or (B) rename the template and solution methods from singFarmSong() to printFarmSong() (and adjust any references such as calls in Main). This alignment will remove ambiguity and ensure students know which method to implement/call.
